answer: At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a tide tag. The yarrow cap is applied at intake and dawn makes public the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a fleet in one epoch however much capital it holds, because every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 23 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
